caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: This figure is a nested donut chart (concentric ring chart) displaying the distribution of samples across two ambiguity measures. The outer ring represents "Ambiguity Std (Outer)" with four slices corresponding to different standard deviation values, while the inner ring represents "Max Ambiguity (Inner)" with three slices corresponding to different maximum ambiguity values. In the outer ring, the largest slice is "Std: 0.0" shown in a very dark navy/teal color at 49.0%, followed by "Std: 0.47" in a medium dark blue at 38.0%, then "Std: 0.82" in a darker teal-blue at 7.0%, and "Std: 0.94" in a medium bright blue at 5.0%. In the inner ring, the largest slice is "Max: 2" shown in a medium-light sky blue at 47.7%, followed by "Max: 1" in a slightly darker cyan-blue at 39.0%, and "Max: 3" in a very light, pale blue at 14.2%. Percentage labels are displayed directly on or adjacent to each slice. Two separate legends are provided to the right of the chart: one for the outer ring listing the four standard deviation categories with their corresponding colors, and one for the inner ring listing the three maximum ambiguity categories with their corresponding colors. The slices in both rings appear ordered by their angular position rather than strictly by size, and the color scheme progresses from darker blues for lower ambiguity values to lighter blues for higher values.
